chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the free man: does a bondwoman confer iḥṣān upon him?

He عليه السلام said: “A bondwoman does not confer iḥṣān upon a free man, nor does a slave man confer iḥṣān upon a free woman. A Christian man confers iḥṣān upon a Jewish woman, and a Jewish man confers iḥṣān upon a Christian woman.”

key_terms.الْحُرَّةَ: the free woman; a legally free female
key_terms.الْحُرِّ: the free man; a legally free person
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: the slave man; a male slave
key_terms.تُحْصِنُهُ: confers iḥṣān upon him; establishes legal marital protection

ai.seo_question: Does marriage to a bondwoman or slave establish legal marital protection (iḥṣān) for a free person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on iḥṣān in marriage and clarifies which marital pairings establish that status. It states that marriage between a free person and an enslaved person does not confer iḥṣān in this context, while marriage between a Christian and a Jewish spouse does confer it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4511 - Al-Alaa narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
I asked Imam (as) whether a bondwoman provides legal protection (iḥṣan) for a free man.

Imam (as) said: "A bondwoman does not provide legal protection for a free man, nor does a slave man provide legal protection for a free woman. However, a Christian man provides legal protection for a Jewish woman, and a Jewish man provides legal protection for a Christian woman."
